name: Behind-Back Cable Shrug
description: The behind-back cable shrug uses a low cable pulley with the lifter standing facing away, the cable passing behind the body and grasped with arms behind the torso. This positioning places the trapezius under tension through a unique posterior angle that is difficult to replicate with any other equipment, and it allows the upper traps to work without the anterior deltoids assisting as occurs in front-loaded shrugs.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing away from a low cable pulley. Reach behind and grasp a straight bar or rope attached to the cable. Stand upright with arms behind the torso.
execution.setup_instructions: Set the cable to the lowest position. Use a straight bar attachment that can be held comfortably behind the body. Moderate weight to begin — the position is unfamiliar.
steps: Step 1: Stand upright with cable grasped behind the lower body.
Step 2: Shrug the shoulders straight upward — no rolling, no forward rounding.
Step 3: Elevate as high as possible.
Step 4: Hold 1 second at peak elevation.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the shrug. Inhale on the lowering.
common_mistakes: Rolling the shoulders — shrug straight up, not in a circular motion
Leaning forward — maintain upright posture throughout
safety_considerations: The behind-back position places the shoulder in internal rotation — keep loads moderate
Avoid if you experience shoulder or bicipital tendon pain
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full shoulder depression to full elevation.
coaching_cues: Straight up — not forward or backward
Hold the squeeze at the top
